items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: We had Andrew on sax and clarinet.

ctx.x: Trombone was, uh, Yankee. And his, uh, they only had six pieces. But they didn't make no recording until I take him with us. See, they was trying to, seems like they were trying to double cross him after he got sick, figured he couldn't play anymore. And trying to put Willie Pajot in his place when they went to Mobile. They went down there and they made a failure. So, the man came and told him, says, uh, that wasn't Sam Morgan Band. What do you heard? So, I told him, I said, we'll take you with us. Oh, he didn't…
Which hall was this that was with them? The Blar and Ed Blar Hall?

items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: So then I played with Young Morgan around here for a few years. And after my brother Sam, he was sick, and, uh, he was not able to keep up a band by himself. So then he came over to my brother Isaiah band, Young Morgan

ctx.x: Oh, yes. I've heard of him. Had a brass band.

Had a brass band. And he had charge of the WPA band too some time back. And now, I've taken a few lessons with David Jones. Oh, yeah. I was on tenor saxophone. And I come in to play any different little bands. Well, our first band was then, if I'm not making a mistake, it's the Imperial. Well, Jack August was playing alto saxophone. I was playing the clarinet. Willie Webber was playing trumpet. And Dr. Bechier, who was that? Oh, yeah. He played trombone? Oh, he was playing trombone. I knew him very well. Yeah.…
that straight. It wasn't that part of Sam's band. Yeah. Well, that's before we joined the band
